misconceptions.claim: An intrusion prevention system makes detection unnecessary.
misconceptions.correction: Prevention can fail, be bypassed, or block legitimate activity; independent detection supports visibility and investigation.

misconceptions.claim: A control is effective because it was installed.
misconceptions.correction: Effectiveness requires operation, coverage, maintenance, health monitoring, testing, and a response path.

outcome: Given a threat and control objective, classify preventive, detective, corrective, and compensating measures, then define how they are operated, monitored, and tested.

sections.body: Preventive measures make an unwanted action harder or less likely, such as segmentation, secure configuration, access control, or filtering. Detective measures identify activity or deviation, such as intrusion detection, endpoint telemetry, integrity monitoring, or review. Corrective measures restore or repair; compensating measures provide a different path to reduce risk when the preferred control is unavailable. Controls can have multiple effects, but the intended purpose and operating evidence should be explicit.
keyPoints: A control type describes its risk-reduction role, not its product category.
Detective measures only help when alert ownership, triage, and response exist.
Compensating controls need documented rationale, scope, duration, and validation.
sections.title: Match control type to the threat

sections.body: Operational controls degrade through drift, disabled agents, changing traffic, new threats, false positives, and staff turnover. Maintain signatures and rules, validate coverage, monitor health, protect management interfaces, test fail-safe behavior, and review performance indicators. Network and host controls should be layered so one missed detection or bypass does not expose the protected asset without another opportunity to contain or alert.
keyPoints: Control health and coverage are operational signals worth monitoring.
False positives consume response capacity; false negatives can conceal harm, so tuning should use risk and evidence.
Layering controls across host, network, identity, application, and data boundaries improves resilience.
sections.title: Maintain and tune controls

summary: Preventive controls reduce the chance or impact of an unwanted action; detective controls reveal events or deviations so people or automation can respond. Operations must maintain, tune, test, and connect both types to a response path.

assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Preventive, detective, corrective, and compensating describe control roles rather than product categories. A compensating sensor should be credited only for the coverage it can actually observe and block.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A coverage map would reveal which behaviors each preventive or detective control sees and which gaps remain; the opening server/agent/sensor grouping does not.
